title: Machine file and post: CNC-STEP S-720 with WinPCNC (mm, manual tool change)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Request

A user (Discord: motley) has a CNC-STEP S-720 desktop mill and wants to post from CamCraft instead of another CAM program. CamCraft has no machine file and no post for this machine or its control software.

## The machine (from the owner)

- CNC-STEP S-720 (High-Z class), 3 axes. Travel X 720 mm, Y 420 mm, Z 110 mm.
- Maximum feed 1259 mm/min.
- Spindle: Kress 1050 FME, 26,300 rpm maximum. The owner did not say if the control sets the speed (the FME has a manual speed dial). Treat S as optional until the manual says otherwise.
- No automatic tool change: a tool change is a manual stop (M0 or the control's own manual-change sequence).
- Control software: WinPCNC Professional, version 4 (Burkhard Lewetz). An interface box connects to the PC over a serial line (USB adapter).
- Units: mm only.

## Work

1. Get the WinPCNC programming documentation from the maker (public download, or the owner sends it with the maker's consent). Read only the maker's manual. Do not use the output or the post of another CAM product (clean-room rules).
2. Add a machine file `cnc-step-s720.mch` with the travels, the feed limit and the spindle range above.
3. Add a WinPCNC post (or a WinPCNC variant of an existing post) for the G-code subset that the manual documents: units, G0/G1/G2/G3, plane, tool change as a manual stop, spindle on/off, comments, program end.
4. Add golden tests for one 2D and one 3D example from the catalog.

Done means: CamCraft posts a WinPCNC program for the S-720 that the maker's manual supports, pinned by golden tests, and the owner can test it on air.
